    The function `spinning_lock_kernel` is a Triton kernel that performs a reduction operation using a spinning lock 
    mechanism for synchronization. This kernel takes input pointers `P`, `C`, and `locks`, with integer parameters 
    `num_sms`, `k`, `M`, `N`, `stride_cm`, and `stride_cn`, and two compile-time constants `BLOCK_SIZE_M` and 
    `BLOCK_SIZE_N`. Each block is identified by a unique program id `pid`, which determines its position in a virtual 
    grid through `pid_m` and `pid_n`. The kernel initializes an accumulator `acc` to zeros. It then loops up to 9 times, 
    performing accumulation only for the first thread (when `pid % k == 0`) by iterating over other participating threads 
    and accumulating their data if successful in acquiring the lock via `tl.atomic_cas`. Threads that don't participate 
    directly in reduction (i.e., where `pid % k != 0`) store the accumulated result in `P` and release the lock using 
    `tl.atomic_xchg`. Finally, the results are written to `C` using computed offsets, and a mask ensures that only valid 
    memory locations are accessed. The `spinning_lock` function orchestrates the kernel launch, preparing the execution 
    grid according to `num_sms` and invoking the kernel with the specified block sizes.
